text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kenya's President Daniel arap Moi authorises importation of maize to supplement reserves and feed families hit by drought.
- The car of opposition FORD-Kenya's first vice president James Orengo is burned and several people are injured in violence at civic by-elections in Alego-Usonga constituency in the lake region.
- A man withdraws an appeal against a five-year prison term for fear that the sentence would be changed to one of hanging.
- President Moi appoints three more assistant ministers to the cabinet.
- The high court lifts an injunction restraining the Central Bank of Kenya from selling by public auction the Grand Regency Hotel.
- Two British airlines report a "technical near collision" at Moi airport in Mombasa.
- A private firm owned by chief officers of Mombasa's municipal council is involved in indiscriminate allocation of land -- mainly road reserves, roundabouts and playgrounds.
- Outgoing health minister Joshua Angatia admits that the ministry is riddled with high level corruption and malpractice.
- An Asian businessman is arrested for selling photocopies of application forms for the new generation identity cards in a bid to beat the January 31 deadline for acquiring the cards.
